原文；段号=chunk 序号，回写按它定位）: The campaign contains 31 scenarios divided in upper and lower paths. The first is common to both. After the first, the upper path contains 15 scenarios while the lower one also 15. There are n ot two scenarios identical and most of them are completely different, even the ones depicting the same battle. After the first scenario you follow one or the other path depending on your battlefield results. A victory or a brilliant victory will keep yo u in the upper path. A loss or a tactical victory will send you into the lower. You can come back to the upper path by a brilliant victory. You enter into an upper path scenario depending on the timetable of the campaign, i.e., the following battle acco r ding to date. In this way you may be sent back and forth between the two paths. Any victory is enough to remain in the lower path, but a loss in the lower path will put you out of the campaign. The only exceptions are Mussolini's Rescue and Sevastopol E vacuation, were you continue whatever your result is. These scenarios are especial mission scenarios. The victory should be achieved following an especially prepared strategy. Some players may miss them. It will be no fun to be thrown out of the campa ign for failing to discover them. By the way, I was never able to win a brilliant victory in Mussolini's Rescue and I prepared it!!!

原文；段号=chunk 序号，回写按它定位）: This campaign has b een designed to reflect fast pace, heavy and continuous action. Sevastopol Evacuation is an extreme example of this. You will lose more units in its 4-5 turns than in several other campaigns. The armies are also significantly stronger than in reality. We all know the AI plays awful, so I have to change the scenarios in a way it can at least play a decent game. All the scenarios contain many over strengthened units, entrenchment, leaders, etc. The percentage increases up to almost 100% in the last sce n ario. In many scenarios the player will be allowed to deploy only a fraction of its army. The auxiliary units are very important because they contribute to the balance of power and at the same time provide some sorely needed capabilities. At the same t i me the game becomes more realistic. Successful campaign play requires minimum casualties or you will be out pretty soon. This fact leads to neglect of the auxiliary units and excessive caution concerning the core units. Here you cannot neglect your aux iliary units. You will need every single one of them or you will not win. I regularly reinforced them to keep them alive.

原文；段号=chunk 序号，回写按它定位）: One interesting concept used in this campaign is the idea of "defensive scenarios." There are several of these scenarios in the campaign. The main idea is, the player does not have neither victory nor supply objectives. In orde r to win the player has to keep all the victory objectives held by him at the beginning of the game. If some are lost the player has to retake them to win. Of course, the game is over if the player loses all of them. Mr. Lasse Jensen originally propose d this idea. It was implemented using his excellent editor. You set victory conditions for both players on the same hexes and then you make sure that at least one of your victory hexes is lost. I found out that 3-4 victory scenarios are the best number. One or two are practically lost from the beginning, and the other one-two is/are under very heavy attack. If you set the AI to attack mode and give adequate reinforcements you have a nice game. The lack of supply hexes is used to reduce the number of p layer units.

I sincerely regret if you do not like this kind of scenarios, but everybody is entitled to his own taste.
